front.why: Docs: apps are private to one customer; 'To publish your app, notify our team as described in the Partnering with Front topic.' The verifier flipped a correct pass-1 value.

threads-meta.why: Meta's Threads docs index has a 'Threads MCP server' section (overview, get started, publishing, insights). Rendered in a browser; plain fetches return empty bodies.

discord.why: Discord hosts a live OAuth-protected MCP endpoint on its own domain; its developer docs don't mention it. Ruled vendor-official, noted as undocumented.
Nearly every Discord action runs as a bot; OAuth2 mainly installs the bot and reads identity.
'Verification is required for your app to scale past 100 servers.' Same kind of gate as HubSpot's 25-install cap, so labelled the same way.

dealcloud.why: About 55-60 documented operations, above the rubric's ~50 line for broad.

zendesk.why: Zendesk API tokens are sent through Basic auth (email/token) and are now marked deprecated; there is no separate API-key scheme.

lark-larksuite.why: The tenant/app access token stands for the app's bot identity; labelled bot_token, as for Discord.
Apps for other companies need vendor verification and a listing review. Same rule as HubSpot, Front and Discord.

fanbasis.why: API keys are issued only after an admin approves a request; the API returns 403 'not approved by the Commas admin' otherwise.

dataforseo.why: Free signup gives working credentials, a $1 credit that does not expire and a free sandbox. A non-expiring credit is not a time-limited trial.

neo4j.why: Database access is Basic or an SSO bearer token; OAuth2 exists only as client credentials for the Aura management API, not as user sign-in.
'Neo4j MCP for Aura is a hosted MCP server for your Aura instances.'
Free Aura tier with no card, public docs, no review step.

ipayx.why: Some routes and the MCP tool list answer without a key. The vendor's own pages contradict each other, so this one is low confidence either way.

quickbooks.why: Intuit documents GraphQL APIs alongside the REST Accounting API.

notebooklm.why: Google publishes an RPC (gRPC) reference next to the REST one.
About 11 operations, inside the rubric's 10-50 range.
